candidates.research_question: Does Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) reduce posttest job burnout while controlling for pretest baseline levels?
candidates.estimand: Average Treatment Effect (ATE) on posttest burnout adjusted for baseline burnout score
assumptions: Homogeneity of regression slopes across intervention and control groups
Linear relationship between pretest covariate and posttest outcome
Homogeneity of error variances across treatment conditions (Levene test p > .05)
Normally distributed model residuals (Shapiro-Wilk test p > .05)
diagnostics: Group by baseline interaction test for regression slope homogeneity
Residual normality Q-Q plot and Shapiro-Wilk test
Studentized deleted residuals for outlier detection
strengths: Maximizes statistical power by conditioning on baseline variance
Controls for baseline chance imbalances in randomized trials
Provides an unconfounded conditional treatment effect estimate
limitations: Requires strict homogeneity of regression slopes
Assumes linear relationship between baseline and posttest scores
candidates.expected_interpretation: Intervention effect on burnout reduction after partialling out pre-existing baseline variance.

candidates.method: Raw Posttest Independent Samples t-test / One-Way ANOVA
candidates.research_question: Does ACT group differ from control group on posttest burnout ignoring baseline scores?
candidates.estimand: Unadjusted posttest mean difference between treatment and control
assumptions: Normality of posttest scores within groups
diagnostics: Levene test for equality of variances
limitations: Lower statistical power and larger residual error
candidates.expected_interpretation: Direct comparison of unadjusted posttest scores across intervention groups.

candidates.research_question: Is there a significant Group by Time interaction on burnout from pretest to posttest?
candidates.estimand: Group-by-Time interaction effect (differential change over time)
assumptions: Missing at Random (MAR) or complete longitudinal cases
diagnostics: Boxs M test for covariance matrices equality
Levene test at each measurement occasion
strengths: Directly models trajectories and Group-by-Time interaction
Evaluates both within-subject change and between-group differences
limitations: Can be susceptible to regression to the mean without baseline adjustment
Complete-case listwise deletion can induce attrition bias if dropouts occur
candidates.expected_interpretation: Differential trajectory of burnout reduction across time points as a function of treatment condition.
